articles.title: A staging task that reached production started with a token in the wrong file
articles.excerpt: When a staging job touches production, the first question is usually "why did the job do that?" I think the better question is "why could it?" The answer is often boring. A production token was sittin…
articles.body: When a staging job touches production, the first question is usually "why did the job do that?" I think the better question is "why could it?" The answer is often boring. A production token was sitting in a file the job had no reason to read. A hypothetical example This is a demo scenario, not a client story. Say a team builds an internal workflow that drafts weekly summaries of support tickets for a human to review. It runs in staging against a copy of the data. The task reads a config folder to find the staging database address. In that same folder, someone left an old .env.backup file. It holds a production token from a migration months ago. The task is not malicious. It just loads every file in the folder, and one of them has a credential that works.

articles.title: React Native vs Native Development: What Should Actually Drive the Decision
articles.excerpt: The choice between React Native and native Swift and Kotlin development should never hinge on developer preference or outdated performance myths. It comes down to three operational realities: how tigh…
articles.body: The choice between React Native and native Swift and Kotlin development should never hinge on developer preference or outdated performance myths. It comes down to three operational realities: how tightly your product needs to couple with device hardware, your organization's engineering topology, and your capital efficiency timeline. For most business applications, customer portals, and transaction workflows, React Native unifies product velocity across platforms while preserving native interface fidelity. Pure native development remains the right call when your app is essentially an extension of device hardware or requires uncompromising platform specialization.

articles.body: How we used a shared Telegram room to organize incident evidence, map operational impact, and keep people in control. We built a warehouse shift-handoff workflow with Switch, Telegram, and six role-based AI agents. The goal is to make incident context easier to review and carry from one shift to the next. Important: The warehouse incident in this demo is simulated. It is not connected to a live warehouse system. Why use Switch for a handoff? articles.body: How I Built RecallOps: Connecting Incident Response with Hindsight Memory Introduction In software engineering, production incidents are unavoidable. Applications can fail, servers can become unavailable, databases can experience unexpected issues, and services can behave differently after deployment. However, one problem that engineering teams repeatedly face is not just fixing incidents but remembering how similar problems were solved in the past. When an incident occurs, engineers often spend valuable time searching through old logs, messages, documentation, and previous troubleshooting records. Sometim es, the same problem has already occurred, but its solution is difficult to find.

articles.body: The storied Mobile Suit Gundam series makes another venture into the tabletop world with Gundam Assemble, a new miniatures game experience. In fact, this new game was revealed alongside the Gundam Card Game as a visual companion, so fans got hit with a fun one-two punch of new game teases. Gundam Assemble is available for the first time this fall, with more expansion packs and sets already prepared to release into early next year. After a good chunk of time with the starter set, this game is shaping up to be a fun bite-size brawl compared to some of the other miniature games out there right now. Arguably one of the biggest barriers of entry to miniature wargames is the building and painting aspect. If building is your biggest concern, have no fear with Gundam Assemble.

articles.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
articles.excerpt: The movies might be struggling to recapture the magic, but Star Wars video games are strong with the Force.
articles.body: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences.
articles.author: Fran Ruiz

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero: Where Is the Rest of Godzilla’s Rogues' Gallery?
articles.excerpt: Where is the rest of Godzilla’s rogues' gallery? We take a look at Monster Island's most wanted.
articles.body: Spoilers follow for Godzilla Minus Zero . Godzilla Minus Zero is upon us, and going by the reviews , it looks like the venerable kaiju franchise has another winner on its hands. More than 70 years after his debut, Godzilla continues to be one of the most iconic characters in cinema history. But even though Minus Zero is another strong entry for the King of the Monsters, I couldn’t help but be a little disappointed that the movie continues a frustrating trend that’s plagued the last couple decades of Godzilla movies by only featuring a handful of his monster co-stars. Specifically, King Ghidorah is the antagonist of Minus Zero, once again assuming his role as the Big G’s archenemy.

articles.title: 10 Funniest 'Far Side' Comics About Cows
articles.excerpt: Gary Larson's The Far Side often featured cows in funny situations. Here are the 10 funniest examples
articles.body: From 1980 until 1995, cartoonist Gary Larson wrote and drew The Far Side . It was a single panel comic strip filled with non-sequitur, surreal jokes mostly aimed at adults instead of children, which was unusual for newspaper comics at the time. Also unusual was the fact that, unlike most daily comic strips, The Far Side had no recurring characters. Peanuts has its gang of kids and Garfield has its cast of humans and animals, but every panel of The Far Side introduces new characters and scenarios all aimed at delivering one single joke.

articles.body: So when, years later, an Alliance clerk told Shepard that a fallen marine named Nirali Bhatia “may save more lives in death than she did in life,” Shepard was faced with the decision — the opportunity — to make Nirali’s death count for something. Before the question ended, she was already agreeing. Hand a grieving husband his wife’s body? Or keep her for research that might save more lives down the line? Someone was going to pay for whichever answer I chose. (I knew Shepard would say yes. I also knew, thumbs hovering over the controller, that every part of me wished she wouldn’t.)

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering Star Trek Perfectly Captures the Sci-Fi Show’s Most Brutal Running Joke
articles.excerpt: Lots of Redshirts are going to die
articles.body: Generating creature tokens is a common way to make the most out of your resources in a game of Magic: The Gathering . They can be sacrificed for powerful effects, used to chump block , or amassed to overwhelm your opponent. Cards typically generate tokens of the same color, like white Warriors for Secure the Wastes , green Squirrels for Deranged Hermit , and black Zombies for Ghoulish Procession . Yet numerous cards in Magic: The Gathering Star Trek generate 1/1 red Officer tokens regardless of the base color, from the white Captain Benjamin Sisko to the green MACO Strike Team . The discrepancy is a nod to the sci-fi franchise’s darkest running joke.

articles.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
articles.excerpt: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a a Dec. 3, 2025 confirmation hearing. In October of 2026, Isaacman sat down with Space.com to discuss the future of the space agency.
articles.body: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova later caleld the Tycho supernova with his bare eyes. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago.

articles.body: Another new private rocket is in the works. AST SpaceMobile announced today (Nov. 6) that it's building a reusable rocket called Blacklift to launch its broadband satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO), with first flight targeted in 2028. The news comes just 10 days after Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron , a rocket designed to launch its constellation of 20,000 AI data centers . Cowboy Space is also targeting 2028 for its first liftoff. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owners’ economics in the industry," Abel Avellan, the company's founder, chairman and CEO, said in a statement today .
